senses.gloss:
Ukhā is the regular word or a ‘cooking pot,’ usually
mentioned in connexion with sacrifice, from the Rigveda^1
onwards. It was made of clay (mṛṇ-mayī).^2 See also Sthālī.
1) i. 162, 13. 15; iii. 53, 22; Av. xii. 3,
23; Taittirīya Saṃhitā, v. 1, 6, 3,
etc.
2) Vājasaneyi Saṃhitā, xi. 59; Tait-
drīya Saṃhitā, iv. 1, 5, 4.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 253,
271.
